use-the-registry-with-your-own-provider-.text: Use the registry with your own provider and wallet.

As a Cardano KERI integrator, you want to run registry and open-datum writes on a test network using an API you choose and a wallet whose signing key stays sealed in your vault or on the machine that signs. The current ordinary path uses Koios for raw reads and signed submission, pinned genesis/history for time, and local construction and evaluation. It does not require an ordinary node socket.

This page describes the current source's configuration. A candidate's local checks, hosted gates, release archive and public-network results are separate receipts; these instructions do not claim that a new release or connected preprod run has been accepted.
The bounded registry journey and the deployment tool are run by the project for now. They will take a vault with issue 672, and this page does not teach them until then.

choose-the-network-and-api.text: Your commands read the chain and send signed transactions through the API you choose. The project's own private development chain sits behind an HTTP facade; your commands name your API instead.

Preprod magic is 1, and the reviewed packaged preprod recording is the default time source there. The generated network's magic is 42, and its launcher supplies its exact published time directory. A supplied directory contains time-manifest.json, shelley-genesis.json and era-history.cbor; their raw identities, network, system start and protocol-major pin are validated. Unsupported time networks refuse rather than borrowing another recording. Writes refuse mainnet.
The old --backend and --node-socket settings are refused on every command. A socket accepted by a separate private probe is a test-harness setting, not an ordinary provider route.

check-the-archive-and-build-its-commands.text: Check the archive and build its commands.
For an existing published archive, verify the bytes and validator identities before using it:

The archive's command interface depends on its revision. An older node-backed archive does not acquire this interface from reading this page. The archive guide records its runnable components and unverified legacy surfaces. Build the registry and naming blueprints from that tree and export REGISTRY_BLUEPRINT and NAMING_BLUEPRINT as the guide specifies. The extracted archive's own singular reads the registry page from its blueprint and the adjacent version file; the Demo 1 run page reads the page right after create with the command the create receipt printed.

make-a-wallet-and-fund-it.text: Make a wallet and fund it.

Make a wallet with singular wallet create, giving --network-magic 1 for preprod. It seals a fresh signing key in an encrypted vault and prints the wallet's address. At a terminal it asks for the passphrase twice, an entry and a confirmation, and refuses a confirmation that differs; in a script, --passphrase-fd FD supplies it as one line read once. singular wallet address asks once, and prints the same address again from the vault.

Fund that address from the preprod faucet so that it holds ordinary outputs, including an ada-only collateral output. A funded balance alone is insufficient when the transaction needs distinct seed, funding and collateral outputs. The Demo 1 run page in the release archive (DEMO1.md) shows the shape the first publication needs and the refusal that names a missing output. A key's bytes do not belong in command output or receipts.

sign-each-write.text: Each write takes exactly one signer. Your own open-datum and singular registry commands sign in one of two ways.
From your vault: add --vault FILE, and --passphrase-fd FD in a script. The command opens the vault once, builds the run, signs it in memory and sends it.

Elsewhere: name the wallet's address with --wallet-address ADDR and a new bundle file with --bundle FILE. The command writes its transactions there and exits with status 19, waiting-for-signatures. Sign the bundle with singular wallet sign --vault FILE and send it with singular submit.
The settings table in the command reference lists the flags of each way, and the Demo 1 run page in the release archive (DEMO1.md) shows both ways from the first command to the last.

how-a-write-is-confirmed.text: A successful submission answer alone is not confirmation. Confirmation requires the exact output. With a validity upper bound the provider deadline is that slot's POSIX start plus 120 seconds; without one it is now plus 300 seconds. Latest-block observation can establish expiry. A refusal, unavailable answer, timeout or mismatching proof stops the run; it is never counted as its intended accepting step.

understand-the-provider-boundary.text: The logical session is Unbound. Its multiple reads may observe different chain states. Facts are Unverified with no configured witness. Raw-source receipts identify what was consumed, but they do not prove the API answered honestly or that all reads were a coherent snapshot. Ledger acceptance remains an independent boundary.

Before construction, the builder selects an interval with at least ten seconds of usable slots at its observed tip. The moving ledger horizon can shorten the upper bound. An empty interval refuses WindowPastLedgerHorizon; a nonempty registry-limited short interval refuses WindowTooShort. Only a horizon-limited otherwise longer window permits one wait for a later horizon, bounded by slots and 20 seconds of wall time. A stalled wait refuses HorizonWaitTimedOut before signing. Build duration can consume the selected interval; this rule is not a guarantee of eventual ledger acceptance.

deployment-and-naming-availability.text: No required hosted workflow currently exercises the legacy deployment-attach script. A compiler or scoped deployment pass does not establish that attached naming is runnable. The retained register-rows, recovery-rows and retirement-rows commands remain unverified under #172 and #283. The recovery and retirement guide documents that design, and the preprod record preserves its historical executed values. This page does not present those naming commands as a current accepted runbook.

Demo 1 has two users, Alice and Bob, starting with empty homes. Neither creates the registry or receives its creation files. Joining by state token is delivered: each joins with the state token, its own wallet and a Koios URL, with no shared directory — every command carries --state-token and no directory option, and neither actor opens the other's files. Joining by reading the registry page generated from the chain is delivered: each reads which registry this is, which release it runs, what its rules are and what it holds, from the token and the packaged release alone, as the registry page describes. Joining by a copied identity file is superseded. Not delivered: a block anchor for the last fold, documentation links checked against a published asset, and the independently derived action identity in the public report. Public replay reconstructs the trie; missing history or a root that does not chain remains a named refusal. Historical deployment and naming receipts remain evidence of their recorded revision and public chain, not a pass for this provider candidate.
